policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'having sent for the disciples' renders μεταπεμψάμενος (send for); προσκαλεσάμενος would be 'having called to him'.
ASV has 'and exhorted them', an unitalicized rendering of παρακαλέσας, which the omission reading lacks.
πορεύεσθαι and πορευθῆναι differ only in tense of the infinitive; ASV 'departed to go into Macedonia' renders either identically.
The added article τὴν before Μακεδονίαν has no English exponent; ASV 'into Macedonia' fits both.
Pure word order (ἐπιβουλῆς αὐτῷ / αὐτῷ ἐπιβουλῆς); ASV 'a plot was laid against him' does not track Greek order.
γνώμης and γνώμη are case variants in the same idiom; ASV 'he determined to return' renders either.
ASV text reads 'as far as Asia' (ἄχρι τῆς Ἀσίας), and its mapped note 'Many ancient authorities omit as far as Asia' marks the omission as the variant, not the text.
ASV names 'the son of Pyrrhus', rendering Πύρρου, which the omission reading lacks.
ASV's adversative 'But these' renders οὗτοι δέ; the omission leaves the contrastive connective unrepresented.
ASV 'had gone before' is προελθόντες; the mapped note 'Many ancient authorities read came, and were waiting' records προσελθόντες as the rejected alternative.
οὗ and ὅπου are synonymous relatives; ASV 'where we tarried seven days' renders either.
ASV 'when we were gathered together' renders the first-person ἡμῶν, not τῶν μαθητῶν ('the disciples').
καθεζόμενος and καθήμενος both mean 'sitting'; ASV 'there sat in the window' renders either.
ASV writes 'had broken the bread' here against anarthrous 'to break bread' in v.7, so the definite article tracks articular τὸν ἄρτον.
ASV 'we, going before to the ship' renders προελθόντες; προσελθόντες would be 'having come to'.
ἐπὶ and εἰς with τὸ πλοῖον both yield ASV 'to the ship'.
Pure word order of the periphrastic διατεταγμένος ἦν; ASV 'so had he appointed' does not distinguish it.
συνέβαλλεν (imperfect) and συνέβαλεν (aorist) both give ASV 'when he met us'; the English past tense does not distinguish aspect here.
ἄντικρυς and ἀντικρύ are orthographic variants of one adverb; ASV 'over against Chios' renders either.
ASV text lacks 'having tarried at Trogyllium' and its mapped note says 'Many ancient authorities insert' it, placing the addition outside the text.
ASV's 'and the day after' is the running connective of a sequence of stages; it does not settle whether δέ stood in the Greek.
ASV 'For Paul had determined' renders the pluperfect κεκρίκει, prior to the narrative; the aorist ἔκρινεν would be 'determined'.
ASV 'if it were possible for him' renders optative εἴη or indicative ἦν alike in English past-conditional form.
ASV reads simply 'and with tears', with no rendering of πολλῶν ('many').
The added article τὸν before θεόν has no English exponent; ASV 'toward God' fits both.
The added article τὴν before the prepositional phrase has no English exponent; ASV 'and faith toward our Lord' fits both.
ASV text reads 'our Lord Jesus Christ', and its mapped note 'Many ancient authorities omit Christ' marks the shorter reading as the variant.
Pure word order (δεδεμένος ἐγὼ / ἐγὼ δεδεμένος); ASV 'I go bound in the spirit' does not track it.
μοι and ἐμοὶ are unemphatic and emphatic forms of one pronoun; ASV 'shall befall me' renders either.
ASV 'testifieth unto me in every city' renders μοι, which the omission reading lacks.
Pure word order of με within 'bonds and afflictions abide me'; ASV does not distinguish it.
λόγου and λόγον are case variants in the idiom οὐδενὸς λόγου/λόγον ποιοῦμαι; ASV 'I hold not ... of any account' renders either.
ASV has one clause, 'But I hold not my life of any account as dear unto myself', with no second negated verb answering οὐδὲ ἔχω.
ASV 'my life' can render articular τὴν ψυχὴν as well as ψυχήν μου; English requires a possessive with 'life' either way.
τελειῶσαι (infinitive) and τελειώσω (subjunctive) after ὡς both give ASV 'so that I may accomplish my course'.
ASV has no 'with joy' rendering μετὰ χαρᾶς in this verse.
ASV reads 'preaching the kingdom' absolutely, with no 'of God' answering τοῦ θεοῦ.
διότι and διὸ are both inferential; ASV 'Wherefore I testify unto you' renders either.
καθαρός εἰμι and καθαρὸς ἐγώ (with copula understood) both yield ASV 'that I am pure'.
The three readings differ only in the placement of ὑμῖν; ASV 'declaring unto you the whole counsel of God' does not track Greek order.
ASV opens 'Take heed unto yourselves' with no inferential 'therefore' rendering οὖν.

ASV text reads 'the church of the Lord' (κυρίου) and its mapped note 'Some ancient authorities ... read God' marks θεοῦ as the variant; the conflate κυρίου καὶ θεοῦ would add 'and God', which ASV lacks.
Pure word order (αἵματος τοῦ ἰδίου / ἰδίου αἵματος); ASV 'with his own blood' renders either.
ASV reads 'I know that after my departing', with neither 'for' (γὰρ) nor 'this' (τοῦτο).
ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν and ἐξ ὑμῶν ἑαυτῶν are both intensive-reflexive; ASV 'from among your own selves' renders either.
ASV reads 'I commend you to God' with no vocative 'brethren' answering ἀδελφοί.
ASV text reads 'to God' (θεῷ) and its mapped note 'Some ancient authorities read the Lord' places κυρίῳ outside the text.
οἰκοδομῆσαι and ἐποικοδομῆσαι both yield ASV 'to build you up'.

ASV 'to give you the inheritance' has both a recipient and a definite article; τὴν κληρονομίαν supports 'the' with 'you' carried over from the preceding clause, while ὑμῖν κληρονομίαν supports 'you' with an idiomatic 'the'. Neither is excluded.
Pure word order (κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο / ἐγένετο κλαυθμὸς); ASV 'they all wept sore' does not track it.
